meaning.en: To reorganise the army and strengthen military preparedness.
meaning.zh: 整顿军队，筹划武备，加强战备。

examples.zh: 新政权上台后，立即整军经武，准备应对边境冲突。
examples.en: Once the new regime took power, it at once set about rebuilding its army to meet border clashes.

examples.zh: 历史上许多王朝都是在整军经武之后才得以中兴。
examples.en: Many dynasties in history were revived only after they had reorganised and re-armed their forces.

usage.en: Formal and literary; mostly used in historical or military writing as a predicate.
usage.zh: 书面语，多用于历史或军事文章，作谓语。

meaning.en: To hold power so great that it dominates the whole country.
meaning.zh: 权势极大，压倒天下所有的人。

equivalents: have the whole country in one's grip

examples.zh: 这位宰相权倾天下，连皇帝也要让他三分。
examples.en: The chancellor wielded such power that even the emperor deferred to him.

examples.zh: 他并不满足于富甲一方，还想权倾天下。
examples.en: He was not content to be the richest man in the region; he wanted to dominate the whole country.

usage.en: Usually carries a disapproving tone, hinting at abuse of power; often used of ministers, eunuchs or tycoons. Predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 多含贬义，暗示滥用权力；常用于权臣、宦官或巨头。作谓语、定语。

meaning.en: To have gone through many worries and hardships in life.
meaning.zh: 饱受、经历了许多忧愁和苦难。

examples.zh: 奶奶饱经忧患，却始终保持着乐观的心态。
examples.en: Grandma has been through a great deal of hardship, yet has always stayed cheerful.

examples.zh: 那一代人饱经忧患，格外珍惜今天的生活。
examples.en: That generation went through so much that they cherish life today all the more.

usage.en: Describes a person (often an older one) who has lived through hard times; neutral to sympathetic. Mostly predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 形容人（多为老人）历尽艰难，中性偏同情。多作谓语、定语。

meaning.en: Full of energy and enthusiasm; in very high spirits.
meaning.zh: 精神非常饱满，干劲十足。

examples.zh: 睡了一个好觉，他今天精神百倍。
examples.en: After a good night's sleep he is in tip-top form today.

examples.zh: 听到胜利的消息，战士们顿时精神百倍。
examples.en: On hearing the news of victory, the soldiers were suddenly full of vigour.

usage.en: A set phrase rather than a classical chengyu; commonly written as a predicate, often after 顿时 or 显得. Positive.
usage.zh: 属固定词组，非典型成语；多作谓语，常与“顿时”“显得”连用。褒义。

meaning.en: Gongs and drums sounding together, as in battle or a festive celebration.
meaning.zh: 锣鼓一齐响起，形容战场上或喜庆场合声势浩大。

equivalents: a roar of drums and gongs

examples.zh: 一声令下，金鼓齐鸣，大军向敌阵冲去。
examples.en: At the command, gongs and drums sounded together and the army charged the enemy line.

examples.zh: 庙会当天，金鼓齐鸣，十里八乡的人都赶来看热闹。
examples.en: On temple-fair day the gongs and drums rang out and people came from miles around.

usage.en: In old military usage 金 is the gong (signal to retreat) and 鼓 the drum (to advance). Now used for lively scenes, with a literary flavour.
usage.zh: 古代军中“金”指锣（鸣金收兵），“鼓”指战鼓（击鼓进军）。今多形容热闹场面，带书面色彩。

meaning.en: To give up a line of work, especially a shady or risky one, for good.
meaning.zh: 指不再干某种行当（多指不正当或危险的行当）。

examples.zh: 他发誓从此洗手不干，老老实实做点小生意。
examples.en: He swore to quit for good and make an honest living from a small business.

examples.zh: 这行当风险太大，我早就洗手不干了。
examples.en: The trade is too risky; I washed my hands of it long ago.

usage.en: Colloquial, often about crime or gambling, but can be used humorously for any job. Compare 金盆洗手, which is more ceremonial.
usage.zh: 口语，多指犯罪、赌博等行当，也可戏指任何工作。较“金盆洗手”更口语化。

natural: cut the mat and end the friendship

meaning.en: To break off a friendship because the other person's values do not match one's own.
meaning.zh: 比喻与朋友绝交，因为志趣、品行不同。

examples.zh: 发现他品行不端后，我决定与他割席断交。
examples.en: After discovering his poor character, I decided to cut all ties with him.

examples.zh: 两人因理念不合而割席断交，多年不相往来。
examples.en: The two split over a clash of principles and had no contact for years.

story.en: Guan Ning and Hua Xin were hoeing a vegetable plot when they turned up a lump of gold. Guan Ning ignored it like a tile; Hua Xin picked it up and then threw it down. Later Hua Xin left his reading to watch a noble's carriage go by, while Guan Ning carried on. Guan Ning cut their shared mat in two and said, 'You are no friend of mine.'
story.zh: 管宁、华歆一起锄地，见到金片，管宁挥锄不顾，华歆拾起又丢下。后来有贵人乘车经过，华歆放下书出去观看，管宁便割断坐席，说：“子非吾友也。”

usage.en: Literary; the story is a classic of friendship-testing. Used of a deliberate break on principle, not a casual quarrel.
usage.zh: 书面语；典故是考验友情的名篇。指因原则分歧而有意绝交，不是一般的吵架。

natural: suspect the neighbour of stealing the axe

meaning.en: To suspect someone without evidence, so that everything about them looks guilty.
meaning.zh: 比喻无根据地猜疑别人，结果看什么都可疑。

equivalents: see guilt in everything a suspect does

examples.zh: 没有证据就疑邻盗斧，只会伤了同事间的和气。
examples.en: Suspecting a colleague with no evidence will only damage goodwill.

examples.zh: 他丢了钱包，便见谁都像小偷，真是疑邻盗斧。
examples.en: Having lost his wallet, he took everyone for a thief — a real case of suspecting the neighbour.

story.en: A man lost his axe and suspected his neighbour's son: his walk, his look and his speech all seemed those of a thief. Later he found the axe in a valley, and the neighbour's son then looked quite innocent.
story.zh: 有人丢了斧子，怀疑邻居的儿子，看他走路、神色、言谈都像偷斧子的。后来在山谷中找到斧子，再看邻居的儿子，就一点也不像了。

usage.en: Warns against prejudice: once you have a suspicion, you read everything as proof. Predicate or standalone comment.
usage.zh: 警示偏见：心里先有怀疑，就把一切都看成证据。多作谓语或独立评语。

meaning.en: To win over an opponent by repeatedly capturing and releasing him until he submits willingly.
meaning.zh: 比喻对对手采取攻心之策，使其心悦诚服。

examples.zh: 谈判中他七擒孟获般地耐心说服对方，终于达成协议。
examples.en: In the talks he patiently won the other side round, Zhuge Liang style, and finally reached an agreement.

examples.zh: 管理者要有七擒孟获的耐心，才能让倔强的下属真心服气。
examples.en: A manager needs the patience of 'seven captures of Meng Huo' to win a stubborn subordinate over sincerely.

story.en: In the southern campaign, Zhuge Liang captured the tribal leader Meng Huo and let him go seven times, until Meng Huo said sincerely that the south would never rebel again.
story.zh: 诸葛亮南征，七次擒获南蛮首领孟获，又七次释放，最终孟获心悦诚服，誓不再反。

usage.en: From the Three Kingdoms story; the point is winning over by persuasion, not force. Also seen as 七纵七擒. Often used in a figurative sense.
usage.zh: 出自三国故事，要点是以德服人、攻心为上。亦作“七纵七擒”。多用比喻义。

natural: hear Shao and forget the taste of meat

meaning.en: To be so absorbed in beautiful music that one forgets even the taste of food.
meaning.zh: 比喻音乐的艺术魅力极高，使人陶醉。

equivalents: so entranced by music one forgets to eat

examples.zh: 听着这段古琴曲，大家闻韶忘味，久久不愿离去。
examples.en: Listening to this guqin piece, everyone was so enraptured they were reluctant to leave.

examples.zh: 她的演唱让满场观众闻韶忘味。
examples.en: Her singing held the whole hall spellbound.

story.en: 'The Master heard the Shao music in Qi and for three months did not know the taste of meat. He said: I never imagined that music could reach such heights.'
story.zh: “子在齐闻《韶》，三月不知肉味，曰：‘不图为乐之至于斯也。’”

usage.en: Praises music (or other art) of great beauty. Literary; the original line is 三月不知肉味. Predicate.
usage.zh: 称赞音乐等艺术极美。书面语；原文为“三月不知肉味”。多作谓语。

meaning.en: To labour at something impossible, in the end achieving nothing.
meaning.zh: 比喻做根本办不到的事，白费力气。

examples.zh: 没有技术就想仿制芯片，无异于猴子捞月。
examples.en: Trying to copy chips without the technology is like monkeys scooping up the moon.

examples.zh: 把希望寄托在一夜暴富上，不过是猴子捞月一场空。
examples.en: Pinning hopes on getting rich overnight is just monkeys grabbing at the moon.

usage.en: From a children's fable (a monkey sees the moon in a well and tries to fetch it). Close in sense to 水中捞月 but more playful and tied to the story. Predicate.
usage.zh: 出自寓言（猴子见井中月影，欲捞取）。与“水中捞月”意近，但更口语、带故事色彩。作谓语。

meaning.en: To have something lost or gone away return; also praise for an honest official under whom prosperity returns.
meaning.zh: 比喻失去的东西复得，或离去的人、物重返；也赞扬官吏清廉、地方复兴。

examples.zh: 流失海外的文物终于合浦珠还，回到了故土。
examples.en: The cultural relics that had been lost abroad have finally come home.

examples.zh: 这位县令一上任，百姓安居，真可谓合浦珠还。
examples.en: With this magistrate in office, the people settled again — truly the pearls returned to Hepu.

story.en: Hepu was famed for pearls, but greedy officials over-harvested them and the oysters migrated away. When Meng Chang became governor and removed the abuses, the pearls came back within a year.
story.zh: 合浦盛产珍珠，因官吏贪婪滥采，珠蚌迁往他处。孟尝任太守后革除弊政，不到一年，珠蚌又回到了合浦。

usage.en: Literary; used of lost treasures returning, or of renewed prosperity. Often seen in headlines about repatriated relics.
usage.zh: 书面语；用于失物复得或地方复兴。常见于文物回归的新闻标题。

meaning.en: Not ideal, but just enough to be some comfort.
meaning.zh: 大体上还可以使人得到一点安慰。

examples.zh: 今年收成虽不算好，但比去年强些，差可告慰。
examples.en: This year's harvest is not good, but it beats last year's, which is some comfort.

examples.zh: 儿子虽未考上名校，成绩尚可，差可告慰。
examples.en: My son did not get into a top school, but his results are decent, which is a small consolation.

usage.en: Understated and slightly formal; 差 here is 'barely, just' (chā kě = 'only just'), so do not read it as 'bad'. Often in letters or reflections.
usage.zh: 语气含蓄，略正式；“差”在此指“勉强、略微”，不是“差劲”。常见于书信或感想中。

meaning.en: To appear and disappear unpredictably, with no fixed pattern.
meaning.zh: 时隐时现，行踪不定，没有规律。

examples.zh: 山里有野猪出没无常，夜间行路要小心。
examples.en: Wild boar roam these hills unpredictably, so take care when walking at night.

examples.zh: 这只流浪猫出没无常，谁也摸不清它的行踪。
examples.en: The stray cat comes and goes as it likes and no one knows where it is.

usage.en: Applies to animals, bandits, spirits or elusive people; as predicate or attributive. 没 here is mò ('vanish'), not méi.
usage.zh: 可指动物、盗匪、鬼神或行踪不定的人；作谓语、定语。“没”读 mò，不读 méi。

meaning.en: The most intelligent of all creatures, that is, human beings.
meaning.zh: 万物中最有灵性、最聪明的，指人类。

examples.zh: 人是万物之灵，更应该善待自然。
examples.en: Humans are the crown of creation and ought to treat nature kindly.

examples.zh: 作为万物之灵，我们却常常做出最愚蠢的事。
examples.en: As the 'most intelligent of creatures', we often do the stupidest things.

story.en: 'Heaven and Earth are the parents of all things; of all things, man is the most spirited' (惟天地万物父母，惟人万物之灵).
story.zh: “惟天地万物父母，惟人万物之灵。”

usage.en: Always refers to humankind; sometimes used ironically when people behave foolishly. Noun phrase, often as apposition.
usage.zh: 专指人类；人做蠢事时有时带讽刺意味。名词性，常作同位语。

meaning.en: For all lifetimes to come, in life after life.
meaning.zh: 生了又生，世世代代，指永远。

examples.zh: 她许愿与丈夫生生世世做夫妻。
examples.en: She vowed to be her husband's wife in every lifetime.

examples.zh: 这份恩情，我生生世世都不会忘记。
examples.en: I will never forget this kindness, in this life or any other.

usage.en: Buddhist-flavoured idea of rebirth; used for oaths of love or gratitude. Typically adverbial. Not the same as 世世代代 (generations of descendants).
usage.zh: 带佛教轮回色彩；多用于爱情或感恩的誓言。常作状语。与“世世代代”（子孙后代）不同。

natural: hurt people as the words leave the mouth

meaning.en: To say hurtful things to others; to insult people.
meaning.zh: 一开口就说伤害别人的话。

examples.zh: 他一生气就出口伤人，事后又后悔不已。
examples.en: Whenever he is angry he says hurtful things, then regrets it bitterly.

examples.zh: 吵架时请克制，不要出口伤人。
examples.en: In an argument, hold back and don't say hurtful things.

usage.en: Disapproving; usually a predicate or a warning. A little more everyday than 恶语伤人.
usage.zh: 贬义；多作谓语或劝诫语。比“恶语伤人”更日常。

natural: hard to fathom the human heart

meaning.en: It is hard to know what is in another person's mind.
meaning.zh: 人的内心想法很难揣测。

equivalents: you never know what people think

examples.zh: 人心难测，合作前最好先看看对方的信用。
examples.en: You can never tell what is in people's minds, so check your partner's reputation before working together.

examples.zh: 他表面热情，其实人心难测。
examples.en: He looks warm on the surface, but who knows what he is thinking.

usage.en: A proverb-like four-character comment, often a sigh about betrayal or hidden motives. Often used on its own.
usage.zh: 类似格言的四字评语，常用来感叹背叛或居心叵测。多单独成句。

meaning.en: Orphans and widows; the weak and helpless left without a family provider.
meaning.zh: 失去父亲的孩子和失去丈夫的妇女，泛指无依无靠的弱者。

examples.zh: 慈善机构每年都会走访孤儿寡妇，送去衣物和食品。
examples.en: The charity visits orphans and widows each year with clothes and food.

examples.zh: 他不忍欺负孤儿寡妇，把欠账一笔勾销了。
examples.en: He could not bear to press orphans and a widow and wrote off the debt.

usage.en: Traditional image of the vulnerable, often tied to the idea that a good ruler cares for them. Neutral to sympathetic. Noun phrase.
usage.zh: 传统上指弱势群体，常与“明君体恤”的观念相联系。中性偏同情。名词性。

meaning.en: Literally a cold-blooded animal; figuratively a heartless, unfeeling person.
meaning.zh: 本指体温随环境变化的动物；比喻冷酷无情的人。

examples.zh: 爬行动物都是冷血动物，体温随气温变化。
examples.en: Reptiles are all cold-blooded animals whose body temperature follows the weather.

examples.zh: 你怎么能对朋友的遭遇无动于衷？简直是冷血动物！
examples.en: How can you be so unmoved by your friend's misfortune? You are a cold fish!

usage.en: Has a biological meaning (neutral) and a figurative insult (strongly negative); watch the context. Noun.
usage.zh: 既有生物学意义（中性），又有比喻义（强烈贬义），注意语境。名词。

natural: free the people hanging upside down

meaning.en: To rescue the people from extreme suffering.
meaning.zh: 把百姓从极端困苦的处境中解救出来。

examples.zh: 义军起兵，志在推翻暴政，解民倒悬。
examples.en: The rebels rose to overthrow tyranny and deliver the people from misery.

examples.zh: 为官一任，当以解民倒悬为己任。
examples.en: An official should make it his mission to relieve the people's suffering.

story.en: Mencius said that if a true king ruled, the people would be as delighted as if released from hanging upside down (犹解倒悬也).
story.zh: 孟子说，施行仁政，百姓的喜悦就如同解除了倒悬之苦（犹解倒悬也）。

usage.en: Used in political and historical contexts for liberators or good officials. Formal, literary; often object of 为 / 以.
usage.zh: 用于政治、历史语境，称颂解放者或好官。正式、书面；常与“为”“以”搭配。

natural: with no regard for head or face

meaning.en: Relentlessly, all over, with no letting up (of beating or scolding).
meaning.zh: 毫无顾忌地、不分头脸地（打、骂等）。

examples.zh: 他被老板没头没脸地骂了一顿。
examples.en: He got a thorough dressing-down from the boss.

examples.zh: 雨点没头没脸地砸下来，我们躲都来不及。
examples.en: The rain beat down on us from all sides and we couldn't dodge it.

usage.en: Colloquial adverbial, usually with 打、骂、砸. Not to be confused with 没头没脑 (abrupt, without rhyme or reason).
usage.zh: 口语状语，常与“打、骂、砸”连用。注意与“没头没脑”（莫名其妙）区别。

meaning.en: To take on a completely new look.
meaning.zh: 面貌完全改变，呈现出新的样子。

equivalents: take on a whole new look

examples.zh: 经过整修，老街面目一新。
examples.en: After renovation the old street has a completely new look.

examples.zh: 新班子上任后，公司面目一新。
examples.en: Under the new management, the company is transformed.

usage.en: Describes places, organisations or atmospheres; positive. Do not mix with 耳目一新, which is about fresh impressions.
usage.zh: 形容地方、单位、气氛，褒义。注意与“耳目一新”（给人新鲜感）区别。
